signals.title: useOfflineSupport.processQueue reports isComplete:true after a head-of-line-blocked (halted) sync cycle
evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:360-375 — on a *retryable* failure the FIFO drain intentionally halts: it sets haltedProgress {current: i+1, failed, isComplete: false} (:367-372), calls onProgress, and `break`s out of the for-loop. The comment (:361-366, issue #1767) documents that the failed action and all successors are carried forward for the next reconnect.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:424-426 — but after the loop there is NO early return on the halted path: control falls straight through to `const finalProgress: SyncProgress = { total, current: total, failed, isComplete: true }` which is set + emitted via setSyncProgress/onProgress UNCONDITIONALLY, immediately overwriting the halted `isComplete:false` signal. So a partially-drained cycle reports to the UI as fully complete (current === total, isComplete: true).

frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:399-416 — the `failed` counter reported in finalProgress excludes the carried-forward retryable items (they are neither in succeededIds nor terminalFailureIds and are re-persisted to QUEUE_KEY at :413-415). Net effect: the sync banner shows 'complete, N failed' while additional actions silently remain queued, so the user believes the offline queue fully flushed when it did not. Fix: `return { success, failed }` on the halt branch (or guard the finalProgress block so it is skipped when the loop broke early). Confidence medium — bug is unambiguous from source; exact UI copy impact not runtime-confirmed.

signals.title: ThreadDetailScreen.handleSend: send-message mutation has onSuccess only, no onError — failed sends are silent
evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/screens/messages/ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:139-142,152-163 — `sendMessage` (useApiMutation POST /api/v1/messages/threads/{id}/messages) is invoked via sendMessage.mutate({content}, { onSuccess: () => { setDraft(''); refetch(); } }). There is NO onError callback and the component never reads sendMessage.isError anywhere. On a 5xx/network failure the message just fails to post with zero user feedback (no Alert/toast/inline error).

Because the draft is cleared only in onSuccess, on failure the draft text is retained but the user gets no signal it didn't send — they may assume it was delivered or re-tap send repeatedly. This is a chat send path, where silent drop is directly user-visible correctness.

Contrast with the segment's other write paths which DO surface errors: LeaseSignatureScreen.tsx:162-165 (onError -> Alert.alert(t(errorKey), err.message)) and VoteDetailScreen.tsx:233-234 (onError -> Alert.alert). ThreadDetailScreen is the outlier. Fix: add an onError that surfaces err.message (Alert or inline banner) and/or render a retry affordance keyed off sendMessage.isError.

signals.title: mobile: empty/error/loading state strings hardcoded in English across ~18 screens despite react-i18next being wired
evidence: react-i18next IS configured and used app-wide (50 files call t()/useTranslation; many screens such as LeaseSignatureScreen and VoteDetailScreen are fully translated), but only 23 of 41 screen .tsx files import useTranslation — the remaining ~18 render hardcoded English, concentrated in list/empty/error/loading fallbacks that sk/cs/de users will see untranslated.

Representative hardcoded user-facing strings (not wrapped in t()): FaultsListScreen.tsx:185,195 ('Loading…','No faults found'); BuildingsScreen.tsx:126,136,137 ('Loading…','No buildings','No properties are linked to your account yet.'); MetersScreen.tsx:156,171,172 ('No unit linked','No meters', body copy); MessagesScreen.tsx:134,141,147 ('Loading…','Try again','No conversations'); ThreadDetailScreen.tsx:174,183 ('← Messages','Loading…'); AnnouncementsScreen.tsx:266 ('No announcements'); WidgetSettingsScreen.tsx:90,163.

Impact: low — i18n/consistency gap, no functional break. The primary/happy-path copy on these screens is often translated, so users get a jarring mix of translated content with English empty/error states. Fix: wrap the empty/error/loading Text nodes in t(...) and add the keys to the mobile locale bundles; add a lint guard (biome/custom) for bare visible <Text> literals in screens/.

signals.title: useOfflineSupport: transient (5xx/network) queued actions are permanently DROPPED after 3 retries with only console.error — silent loss of offline-created content
evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:353-357 — the catch branch increments action.retries (:353) then `if (isPermanent || action.retries >= 3)` (:354) adds the action to terminalFailureIds and logs `console.error('Action failed after max retries:', action)` (:357). Dropping the 4xx-`permanent` case is correct, but bundling *transient* failures (5xx / network — the comment at :350-352 explicitly routes '5xx, network' through the retry budget) into the SAME terminal drop means a queued mutation that hit 3 consecutive server-5xx / connectivity blips is discarded, not carried forward.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useOfflineSupport.ts:399-401 — carriedForward = queue.filter(a => !succeededIds.has(a.id) && !terminalFailureIds.has(a.id)); anything in terminalFailureIds is excluded from `merged` and thus deleted from QUEUE_KEY on the subsequent AsyncStorage.setItem. The action is gone from local storage; nothing re-enqueues it.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/App.tsx:81-83,337 — the sync toast's ONLY recovery affordance is onRetry={handleRetrySync}, and handleRetrySync (:81-83) just calls processQueue() again. Because the terminally-dropped action is no longer in the queue, tapping Retry cannot recover it. For offline-created user content (a queued fault report, meter reading, vote, or acknowledgement made while offline) this is silent data loss after transient server unavailability, with no user-facing record of what was lost (only a console.error a phone user never sees).

Distinct from the pass-A 'offline-sync-false-complete' finding (about the isComplete:true flag on the halted path, useOfflineSupport.ts:424-426). This is a separate failure mode: permanent discard of transient-failed actions at :354-357. Suggested fix: treat only isPermanent (4xx) as terminal; give transient failures a larger bounded budget or move them to a dead-letter store surfaced in the UI rather than deleting them. Confidence medium — data-loss path is unambiguous from source; exact field impact depends on which action types reach retries>=3.

signals.title: usePushNotifications: debug console.log left on the device-token register/unregister production path
evidence: frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/usePushNotifications.ts:240 — console.log('[push] registering native device token with backend') and :267 — console.log('[push] unregistering native device token with backend') are plain debug logs on the always-run push-registration path, not gated behind __DEV__ or a logger abstraction.

Contrast with the rest of the segment, whose logging is exclusively console.warn/console.error inside catch blocks (useOfflineSupport.ts, NFCCredentialManager.ts, backgroundNotifications.ts, AuthContext.tsx). These two console.log calls are the only informational debug logs left on a hot production path.

Impact: low — no functional break; release-log noise and a lint/hygiene smell. Fix: remove them or route through the app logger gated on __DEV__. Grouped here only as the one net-new hygiene item not covered by prior mobile-rn passes.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/lib/queryKeys.ts:347 — AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS is the allow-list logout() iterates to purge session-scoped TanStack Query subtrees (contexts/AuthContext.tsx:553-555: `for (const root of AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS) queryClient.removeQueries({ queryKey: [root] })`). Its own doc (AuthContext logout, issue #712) states the goal is that 'user-bound data never leaks into the next session'. Any query-key root NOT in this list is NOT purged on logout.

Three feature hooks define their own local key factory whose root string is missing from AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS: features/predictive-maintenance/hooks/usePredictiveMaintenance.ts (`predictiveKeys.all = ['predictive-maintenance']`), features/sentiment (`all: ['sentiment']`), features/notification-analytics (`all: ['notification-analytics']`). Static diff: roots defined by feature *Keys factories = {ai-chat, notification-analytics, predictive-maintenance, sentiment}; only 'ai-chat' is present in the allow-list — the other three were forgotten when their pages were routed (gap-sweep, Epic 13 / Story 2B-C.3).

All three are tenant-scoped: predictive-maintenance equipment/prediction lists (`GET /ai/equipment`), sentiment analytics, and notification delivery analytics. All three pages are routed and reachable (routes/lazyRoutes.tsx:317 SentimentDashboardPage, :322 NotificationAnalyticsPage, :336 PredictiveMaintenancePage). ppt-web is an SPA — logout does NOT reload the page, so queryClient persists across logout->next-login. On a shared manager/kiosk workstation, user B navigating to any of these three pages after user A logged out can see user A's cached data until the 5-min staleTime lapses or a refetch completes.

Fix: add 'predictive-maintenance', 'sentiment', 'notification-analytics' to AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS (queryKeys.ts:347). Better: add a CI/lint or unit assertion that every feature-local *Keys.all root is a member of AUTHED_QUERY_KEY_ROOTS so future gap-sweep pages can't silently reintroduce the leak. Distinct from all prior ppt-web-core findings (none touched the logout purge list).

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/App.tsx:229-231 — the entire lazily-loaded route table renders inside `<main><Suspense fallback={<RouteLoading/>}><AppRoutes/></Suspense></main>` with NO React error boundary at the route-outlet level. The ONLY ErrorBoundary in the app is at the root (main.tsx:50, wrapping the whole `<App/>` — every provider, AppNavigation, and the outlet).

routes/lazyRoutes.tsx defines ~90 `lazy(() => import(...))` page chunks (all feature pages). A rejected dynamic import is NOT caught by Suspense — it propagates as a thrown error. After a redeploy, a user holding a stale index.html requests an old hashed chunk that no longer exists on the CDN (404) — a routine production event for a Vite hashed-chunk SPA. That rejection, or any render-time throw inside a page, bubbles to the ROOT boundary and unmounts the entire application shell (nav + layout + providers UI), replacing everything with the global fallback.

components/ErrorBoundary.tsx:99 handleRetry only resets `hasError` and re-renders the same children — for a failed `lazy()` import the browser has permanently cached the rejected module promise, so 'Try Again' re-throws immediately; only the full 'Reload Page' path (window.location.reload, :182) recovers. Net effect: a single failed page chunk or one buggy page component takes down the whole shell with no in-place recovery.

Fix: wrap `<Suspense><AppRoutes/></Suspense>` in App.tsx:229 with a route-scoped `<ErrorBoundary>` (the component already supports a custom `fallback`) so failures are contained to the `<main>` outlet, keeping AppNavigation/shell mounted and letting the user navigate away or retry a single route. Optionally give the route-level boundary chunk-load-error detection that triggers an automatic one-shot reload. Prior 2026-07-24 ppt-web-core note recorded 'ErrorBoundary present' as a positive but did not examine its placement/granularity — this is a new finding.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/rentals.tsx — all four useMutation hooks in the rentals route wrappers omit onError: createConnection (rentals.tsx:258), syncPlatforms (:272), checkIn (:373), checkOut (:385). Each defines only onSuccess (queryClient.invalidateQueries). A failed platform connect/sync or booking check-in/check-out therefore produces NO user-facing feedback — the mutationFn rejects, the query cache is not invalidated, and the UI silently stays as-is; the user cannot tell the action failed vs. is still pending.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/financial.tsx — PaymentManagementPageRoute's matchMutation (financial.tsx:296, manual payment->invoice allocation, onMatch) and autoMatchMutation (:305, bulk auto-match, onAutoMatch) also define only `onSuccess: invalidatePayments` with no onError. A failed allocation/auto-match on a money-movement action gives the manager no error toast.

This is inconsistent with the established convention in the SAME file: sendInvoiceMutation (financial.tsx:169) and downloadPdfMutation (:191) both pair onSuccess with an onError that calls showToast({ type: 'error', ... }). The six mutations above were simply not given the matching error branch. Fix: add an onError handler to each (surface a showToast error, mirroring sendInvoiceMutation:179-186), so mutation failures on these user-initiated write actions are reported rather than swallowed.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/routes/groups/rentals.tsx:169-176 — useRentalsAuth() returns `{ authorization, xTenantId } | null` and explicitly returns null when `!token || !user?.organizationId` (e.g. access token expired / cleared mid-session, since ppt-web is an SPA that does not reload on token loss).

The useQuery call sites guard this correctly with `enabled: !!auth` (rentals.tsx: reservations query :182 enabled at :190, connections query :192 enabled) so the queryFn's `auth!.authorization` (:186-187,:197-198) never runs while auth is null. But useMutation has no `enabled` gate: createConnection (:258), syncPlatforms (:272), checkIn (:373) and checkOut (:385) all dereference `auth!.authorization` / `auth!.xTenantId` (:251-252,:262-263,:276-277 and the checkIn/checkOut header blocks) inside mutationFn. If the user triggers one of these actions after the token has been dropped, `auth!` (non-null assertion on an actually-null value) throws a TypeError at call time instead of yielding a clean auth error.

Fix: null-check auth at the top of each mutationFn (early-return / throw a typed AuthError, or disable the triggering control when `!auth`) rather than relying on the `!` assertion, so a mid-session token loss degrades to a handled error path (and, combined with the onError finding, a toast) instead of an uncaught TypeError. Distinct from prior AuthContext findings — this is the rentals route wrapper's own auth helper usage.

Eight route-wrapper 'entity not found' fallbacks render hardcoded English JSX text with no react-i18next `t(...)` wrapping: routes/groups/announcements.tsx:521 & :596 (`
Announcement not found
`), buildings.tsx:36 (`
Building not found
`), community.tsx:78 (`
Group not found
`), faults.tsx:418 & :472 (`
Fault not found
`), messaging.tsx:172 (`
Thread not found
`), rentals.tsx:399 (`
Booking not found
`).

These are user-facing strings on a real render path (returned when a detail route's id resolves to no entity), so a Slovak/Czech/German user hitting a missing/deleted entity sees untranslated English. The repo standard is i18n via `t('...')` (react-i18next 16, locales sk/cs/de/en) — the same route files use `t()` for their other labels; these fallbacks were left as literals.
Fix: wrap each in `t('common.notFound', { defaultValue: '<Entity> not found' })` (or per-entity keys) and add the keys to the sk/cs/de/en bundles. Low severity (i18n gap, no functional break).
